correctness.rationale: A bi-Lipschitz bijection linearizes to an isomorphism of Lipschitz-free spaces, and every finite-dimensional normed space is linearly isomorphic to Euclidean space. Mason's 2026 theorem, visible already in the primary arXiv abstract, gives the Dunford--Pettis property for \(\mathcal F(M)\) whenever \(M\subset\mathbb R^d\). The Dunford--Pettis property is preserved by countable \(\ell_1\)-sums and complemented subspaces. Godefroy--Kalton's lifting theorem embeds every separable \(X\) as a complemented copy in \(\mathcal F(X)\), so failure of the property for \(X\) forces failure for \(\mathcal F(X)\). The contradiction for a complemented embedding into the sum is therefore valid.

originality.rationale: The submitted statement is mechanically implied by Mason's main theorem together with standard permanence of the Dunford--Pettis property under countable \(\ell_1\)-sums and complemented subspaces and the standard Godefroy--Kalton lifting. Mason's abstract already states the key general consequence that \(\mathcal F(M)\) is not isomorphic to \(\mathcal F(X)\) for every Euclidean-subset model \(M\) and every separable \(X\) failing Dunford--Pettis. Allowing a sequence of such pieces and strengthening the conclusion to exclusion of complemented embeddings is the direct closure-property corollary, not a new obstruction mechanism.

final_claim: If a separable Banach space \(X\) fails the Dunford--Pettis property and every metric space \(M_j\) admits a finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz model, then \((\bigoplus_j\mathcal F(M_j))_{\ell_1}\) has the Dunford--Pettis property while \(\mathcal F(X)\) does not; consequently \(\mathcal F(X)\) cannot be isomorphic to a complemented subspace of that sum.
limitations: Scientific rejection is for originality and value, not correctness.
